title: Card Grading Near Me (2026)
verdict: Card grading near me almost always means mailing cards to a lab, and AGS is the best answer in 2026: drop-off at select locations, or mail-in with a return in 20 business days or less.
Be careful with any shop or kiosk that claims to grade on the spot. Ask whose slab the card comes back in. If it is not a grader buyers recognize, the grade will not help you sell.

list: Go to a card show. Large shows often have graders accepting submissions, and some grade on site at premium prices.
Mail them to a grader yourself. This is how most cards are graded. AGS returns standard orders in 20 business days or less.
Drop them off. AGS accepts in-person drop-offs at select locations, including secure intake at its headquarters at 727 Page Ave, Staten Island, New York. Confirm with AGS first.
Use a card shop. The shop ships your cards to a grading company and adds a handling fee. Ask which grader, which tier and the full price.

sections.h: Ask a shop this before you hand over cards
list: Which grading company and which service tier?
What is the total per card, including your fee?
How are the cards insured on the way there and back?
When will they come back, and can I track the order with the grader?

ranking.fit: Collectors who want to drop cards off in person at a select AGS location, or mail them and have them back in weeks.
ranking.lacks: No walk-in counter in most cities. Confirm intake before you travel.
ranking.note: By mail, the standard service is 20 business days or less from the day cards are confirmed. Returns ship with tracking and optional insurance.

ranking.fit: Budget submitters with 10 or more cards worth under $500 each.
ranking.lacks: No measured report behind the grade.

ranking.fit: Sellers who will mail a valuable card and wait for the best-known label.
ranking.lacks: No local counter. Cards go by mail or through a show.

ranking.fit: Modern card collectors who like the half-point scale.
ranking.lacks: Subgrades by eye, and 45 business days or more at the Base tier.

ranking.fit: Small sellers who would rather not choose a tier.

why: Mail-in is the default everywhere in this hobby, AGS included. The difference is that AGS also takes in-person drop-offs at select locations and runs satellite labs, so some collectors can skip the post office. Confirm the location with AGS first.
You can send one card. AGS has no minimum and no membership fee, takes payment only when the cards are graded, and lets you cancel before grading starts. Bulk pricing begins at 30 cards.

One price covers everything. $18 buys the scan, the grade, eight subgrades, the report and the slab, for any card at any value. Orders of 30 or more TCG cards pay $15 a card on the standard bulk tier.

faq.q: Is there card grading near me?
faq.a: Grading is done in central labs, so near me usually means by mail. AGS returns mail-in orders in 20 business days or less and takes in-person drop-offs at select locations.

faq.q: How long does card grading take?
faq.a: It depends on the grader and the tier. AGS lists 20 business days or less, with 10 and 5 day tiers. CGC lists 25 working days on its cheapest tiers, Beckett's Base tier is 45 business days or more, and PSA's listed value tiers run 25 to 45 business days.
Rarely. Many act as middlemen: they collect cards, batch them, send them to a grading company and add a handling fee. Ask which grader they use, which tier, and what the total will be.

faq.q: Is there a card grading company near me?
faq.a: Probably not one that grades on site. Almost every grader works by mail from one or two labs. A local card shop that offers grading is usually forwarding cards to one of them for a fee.

faq.q: Can I get a card graded the same day?
faq.a: AGS says same-day grading is available for urgent submissions. Contact AGS before you ship or drop off to arrange it. Elsewhere, the quickest posted tiers are 2 to 5 business days and cost $50 to $150 a card.
